title: The History of the Web
passages: The World Wide Web was invented by a British SCIENTIST named Tim Berners-Lee. He was working at CERN, a giant PHYSICS LABORATORY near Geneva, SWITZERLAND. Thousands of researchers there needed a better way to share documents, and in 1989 he wrote a PROPOSAL describing a system to link information together.

His big idea was HYPERTEXT, a way of connecting documents so that clicking a link jumps you straight to another page. To make this INVENTION work he created three things: HTML for writing pages, a method for addresses, and a way for computers to talk to each other. By 1991 the Web was ready for the world.

To read a page you need a BROWSER, the program that fetches a website and shows it on your screen. Berners-Lee wrote the very first one in 1990 and called it WorldWideWeb. It was clever because it could both display pages and edit them, but it only ran on one rare type of computer.

The Web really took off in 1993 with MOSAIC, a GRAPHICAL browser that could show pictures alongside text. Soon after came NETSCAPE Navigator, which became hugely popular. These programs gave people a friendly INTERFACE so that anyone, not just scientists, could explore the Web.

The world's first WEBSITE went live on 6 August 1991 at an address beginning info.cern.ch. It was PUBLISHED on a single computer acting as a SERVER, which is a machine that stores web pages and sends them out when someone asks. The page simply explained what the World Wide Web project was and how to use it.

Early sites were plain pages of text and links, with no fancy colours or animation. Some acted like a DIRECTORY, a tidy list pointing visitors towards other useful pages. From this humble start, the number of websites grew from one to billions in just a few DECADES.

At first, web pages just sat there. To make them come alive, a programmer named Brendan Eich created a new LANGUAGE in 1995 while working at Netscape. He built the first version in only about ten days, and it was eventually given the name JAVASCRIPT.

JavaScript is a SCRIPTING language that runs inside your browser. It lets a page respond when you click, type, or scroll, making it INTERACTIVE instead of still. Today almost every website you visit uses it, which is why it is one of the most important tools a web DEVELOPER can learn.

In the late 1990s, people grew wildly excited about the INTERNET. Hundreds of new COMPANIES were created with names ending in '.com', and they became known as dotcoms. Eager INVESTORS handed them enormous amounts of money, hoping the web would make everyone rich very quickly.

Prices on the stock market climbed into the BILLIONS, even for businesses that earned no PROFIT at all. This swelling of value with little real worth behind it is called a BUBBLE, and in the year 2000 it finally burst. Many dotcoms went BANKRUPT and vanished almost overnight.

HTML is the code used to build every web page, and the rules for it are set by a group called the W3C, short for the World Wide Web CONSORTIUM. Around the year 2000 they tried to replace it with XHTML, a far STRICTER VERSION that punished even tiny mistakes by refusing to display the page.

Many builders found XHTML too rigid, so in 2004 a rival group of browser makers formed the WHATWG. They wanted a more FLEXIBLE STANDARD and created HTML5, which let pages play video, sound, and other MULTIMEDIA without extra add-ons. In time the two groups cooperated, and HTML5 became the modern standard.
